activities.title: Yeast budding in sugar solution
activities.summary: Yeast in glucose solution produces buds visible under microscope — asexual reproduction by budding.

activities.title: Bread mould on wet bread
activities.summary: Wet bread grows mould (hyphae and spores) — compare yeast budding vs mould spore formation.

activities.title: Binary fission in Amoeba
activities.summary: Observe permanent slides of Amoeba and binary fission — unicellular asexual reproduction.

activities.title: Fragmentation in Spirogyra
activities.summary: Filamentous Spirogyra breaks into fragments that grow into new individuals.

activities.title: Spore formation in Rhizopus
activities.summary: Observe bread mould spores in sporangia — asexual reproduction by spores.

activities.title: Vegetative propagation in Bryophyllum
activities.summary: Bryophyllum plantlets on leaf margins grow into new plants — vegetative propagation.

activities.title: Germination of pollen on stigma
activities.summary: Pollen grains germinate on stigma; pollen tubes grow toward ovules.

exercise_mcqs.question: Asexual reproduction takes place through budding in
exercise_mcqs.explanation: Yeast reproduces asexually by budding — a small outgrowth forms and separates. Amoeba uses binary fission.

exercise_mcqs.question: Which of the following is not a part of the female reproductive system in human beings?
exercise_mcqs.explanation: Vas deferens is part of the male reproductive system — it carries sperm. Ovary, uterus, and fallopian tube are female parts.

exercise_mcqs.question: The anther contains
exercise_mcqs.explanation: Anther is the part of stamen (male) that produces pollen grains containing male gametes.

intext_samples.question: What is the importance of DNA copying in reproduction?
options: DNA copying is not needed for reproduction
DNA copying ensures offspring receive complete genetic information for body design
DNA copying only happens in sexual reproduction
intext_samples.explanation: DNA must be copied and passed to new cells so offspring inherit instructions for body design and survival.

intext_samples.question: Why is variation beneficial to the species but not necessarily for the individual?
options: Variation helps species survive environmental changes even if some individuals suffer
intext_samples.explanation: Variations create diversity so some individuals may survive if conditions change — benefits species survival.

intext_samples.question: How does binary fission differ from multiple fission?
options: Binary fission produces many cells; multiple fission produces two
Binary fission splits into two; multiple fission produces many daughter cells at once
Multiple fission occurs only in plants
intext_samples.explanation: Binary fission: one cell → two (Amoeba). Multiple fission: one cell → many (Plasmodium).

intext_samples.question: How is the process of pollination different from fertilisation?
options: Pollination is transfer of pollen to stigma; fertilisation is fusion of gametes
intext_samples.explanation: Pollination moves pollen to stigma; fertilisation fuses male and female gametes inside the ovule.

intext_samples.question: What are the changes seen in girls at the time of puberty?
options: Breast development, menstruation begins, wider hips
Only height increases with no other changes
intext_samples.explanation: Puberty in girls includes breast development, onset of menstrual cycle, and wider hips — driven by oestrogen.

intext_samples.question: How will an organism be benefited if it reproduces through spores?
options: Spores are lightweight, easily dispersed, and survive harsh conditions
Spores always produce identical offspring with no variation
intext_samples.explanation: Spores have thick walls, are light and easily spread by air/water, and survive unfavourable conditions.
